title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes' (surgery of conformal, i.e. Riemann, surfaces, possibly with boundary). The page defines elementary operations meant to be composed into a calculus of surgeries.

(1) Découpage (cutting). Take a conformal surface X, possibly with boundary, and a compact rectifiable 1-dimensional subcomplex K (an embedded finite graph with rectifiable edges). Cutting X along K gives a compact surface with boundary, X̃. Its new boundary ∂'X̃ comes with a marked boundary collar (annulus).

(2) Recollage (regluing). Start from a conformal surface with boundary, a compact collar of the boundary, and an 'admissible' equivalence relation on the boundary (admissible 'in the rectifiable sense'). Typical examples are identifying boundary arcs by arc-length isometries, or collapsing arcs to graphs. The quotient is again a conformal surface, possibly with boundary. Cutting along K and regluing by the tautological relation gives back X.

(3) Rétrécissage (shrinking). Given K ⊂ X, let X̃ be X cut along K and ∂'X̃ the distinguished part of the boundary (the part coming from K).
- Choose a multi-annulus around ∂'X̃, i.e. one collar per boundary component (∂'_i X̃).
- Key remark: a germ of bi-annulus around a component amounts to a 'rectifiable' length structure of total length 1 on that circle. Equivalently, a parametrisation by R/Z up to rotation, which then determines a standard conformal collar {1-ε < |z| ≤ 1}.
- Remove from each component a crown (couronne) of width ε_i. The figure shows hatched collars of widths ε_i, ε_j, with 0 ≤ ε_i < +∞. This gives the shrunken surface X̃*.
- Choose a rectifiable isomorphism ∂'X̃* ≅ ∂'X̃ compatible with the components and carrying the length structures across.
- Transport the gluing relation of ∂'X̃ (the one rebuilding X from X̃) to ∂'X̃*, and reglue. The result is a new conformal surface X* that still contains a copy of K.

The next page adds the inverse operation 'élongation' (inserting a collar), a mixed operation, commutation of operations attached to different components of K, and the real-analytic case. That case reduces to removing a collar around an analytic curve C and regluing by a cylinder.

Purpose. The goal is a canonical way to deform the conformal structure of X while keeping a graph K ⊂ X fixed. Varying the widths ε_i gives real families of conformal surfaces carrying the 'same' graph. This is the type of tool needed to relate graphs on surfaces (maps / dessins, ribbon graphs with lengths) to the moduli spaces M_{g,n}. It fits Grothendieck's 1977–84 programme leading to the Esquisse (dessins d'enfants, Teichmüller tower, 'géométrie modérée').

In modern terms:
- Élongation is Thurston-type grafting: inserting a Euclidean cylinder along a curve.
- Shrinking is its inverse, or a 'pinching' deformation.
- Regluing via boundary equivalence relations is conformal welding.
- The collars of prescribed widths around the cut graph resemble the cylinder decomposition defined by a Jenkins–Strebel differential. Its critical graph is a metric ribbon graph, as in the Harer–Mumford–Thurston/Penner/Kontsevich cell decomposition of M_{g,n} × R_+^n.
errors: A conformal surface carries no lengths, so 'rectifiable' for a 1-complex, a boundary equivalence relation or a boundary isomorphism needs auxiliary metric data. Grothendieck does not specify it (tacitly a tame or Riemannian length class).

The claim that a germ of (bi-)annulus around a boundary component 'amounts to' a length structure of total length 1 is only correct in the real-analytic setting. There, a real-analytic parametrisation of an analytic boundary curve extends uniquely, by Schwarz reflection, to a germ of conformal collar. A merely rectifiable length structure does not determine a conformal collar, nor is it compatible with the conformal structure of X̃. The author's later restriction to 'R-analytique' (next page) acknowledges this.

In regluing, it is not automatic that the quotient carries a conformal structure extending the given ones. Existence is a conformal welding problem: it is fine for analytic or quasisymmetric gluing maps but can fail in general. Uniqueness needs the seam to be conformally removable, which holds for sets of σ-finite length (Besicovitch), presumably why 'rectifiable' is required. These conditions are hidden in the undefined word 'admissible'.

For rétrécissage the widths ε_i cannot range over all of [0, +∞). The removed crown must embed in X̃, so ε_i is bounded by the modulus of a maximal embedded collar. The range 0 ≤ ε_i < +∞ only makes sense for the inverse operation (élongation) or with a different normalisation.
X* depends on the choices of collars and of the boundary isomorphism (up to rotation). The page does not address this dependence, i.e. what is canonical (only up to twist / rotation parameters).

ideas.what: Cutting a Riemann surface along a compact rectifiable graph K to get a bordered surface with marked boundary collars, and regluing by an equivalence relation on the boundary
ideas.modern_name: cut-and-paste of Riemann surfaces; conformal welding
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riemann, Koebe); conformal welding: Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen (1960s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses maps/dessins on conformal surfaces but, to my knowledge, not this surgery calculus explicitly

ideas.what: Shrinking: removing collars of width ε_i around the boundary components coming from K and regluing to get a family X*_ε containing K
ideas.modern_name: inverse grafting / collar-width (modulus) deformation; cylinder-height deformation of Jenkins–Strebel differentials; pinching
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (projective grafting, c. 1980s); Hejhal; Kamishima–Tan (1992); McMullen 'Complex earthquakes' (1998); Strebel (1984) for Jenkins–Strebel cylinders

ideas.what: Correspondence between germs of collars around a boundary circle and normalised length (parametrisation) structures of total length 1
ideas.modern_name: real-analytic boundary parametrisation ↔ germ of conformal collar via Schwarz reflection; 'rigged' Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; rigged surfaces in Segal's CFT axioms (1987–88), Radnell–Schippers

ideas.what: A system of composable elementary surgeries (cut, reglue, shrink, elongate, mixed) on pairs (X, K), with commutation for different components of K
ideas.modern_name: operadic / gluing calculus on moduli of bordered Riemann surfaces with graphs; metric ribbon graph deformations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (CFT, 1987); Penner, Kontsevich (metric ribbon graphs, 1987–92); Harer–Mumford–Thurston cell decomposition
ideas.where_published: Possibly related remarks in Esquisse §3 on surfaces and dessins; nothing equivalent known to me in print

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a systematic surgery calculus for pairs (conformal surface, embedded rectifiable graph). It includes collar-width deformation that keeps the graph fixed, with the aim of composition and commutation laws. This is an early, independent version of grafting / Strebel-cylinder deformations used to link graphs on surfaces to moduli spaces, before or concurrent with Penner/Kontsevich. As a general 'tame' calculus (rectifiable rather than analytic or quadratic-differential based) it seems not to have been developed.
missed.quote: Rétricissage K ⊂ X ... X̃* la surface à bord rétrécie déduite de la couronne ... On en conclut X* et K ⊂ X*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a framework for deforming conformal structures with an embedded graph held fixed, in the spirit of tame geometry. Such a framework could unify grafting, Strebel deformations and welding, and give a geometric route from dessins to M_{g,n}. Historically it documents Grothendieck's pre-Esquisse thinking.

missed.claim: Regluing via an 'admissible equivalence relation on the boundary (rectifiable sense)' is conformal welding. Requiring rectifiability matches the removability theorems that guarantee uniqueness of the welded structure. This links Grothendieck's dessins / Teichmüller programme to welding theory, a link not usually made explicitly in the dessins literature.
missed.quote: une relation d'équivalence "admissible" (au sens rectifiable) sur le bord
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Welding plus removability gives a rigorous foundation for gluing surfaces along graphs, relevant to dessins, ribbon-graph models and CFT sewing.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a programmatic sketch of standard-looking surgery operations, without theorems. The interest is historical: Grothendieck independently formulating collar insertion/removal (grafting-type) deformations that fix an embedded graph, in a 'rectifiable' setting, around 1977–84. Specialists would recognise the operations, but this calculus is not attributed to him in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Découpage d'une surface conforme (évt avec bord) suivant un sous-1-complexe rectifiable compact'.
'un anneau compact des bord' is probably 'un anneau de bord compact' (boundary collar).
The insertion above 'surface' in item 1 is 'compacte' ('une surface compacte à bord').
The parenthesis should read '(un germe de bi-anneau autour d'une composante (∂'_i X̃)_i revient à la donnée d'une structure rectifiable de long. totale 1 sur celle-ci...)'.
The '[?]' insertion near the end is plausibly 'relation d'équivalence' (on ∂'X̃*), i.e. 'pour en déduire une [relation d'équivalence] sur X̃*'.
'X̃ découpé de X suivant K' rather than 'découpe'.
